name: Drekk IronPalm Weld & Chem Work Gauntlet
description:
Heavy-duty gauntlets built for the forge floor and acid-wash bays. Outer shell is heat-scored syn-leather over a nitrile-composite palm, stained amber and grey from sustained chemical exposure. Knuckle ridges are reinforced with stamped recycled ferrosteel plates. The wrist cuff is wide and buckled — designed to seal over jumpsuit sleeves or bare skin alike.

Cutaway index and middle fingers on the dominant hand allow for basic touchpad input without removal. Interior lining is moisture-wicking mesh, replaceable as a separate insert sold by the sheet at most Tier 1–2 hardware stalls.
functionality: Rated for temperatures up to 480°C brief contact. Chemical resistance against common industrial acids and solvents. Reinforced palm reduces vibration fatigue from pneumatic tools. Cutaway fingers allow limited terminal input without full removal.
what_it_says: You work with your hands in places that would ruin someone else's skin, and you don't expect anyone to thank you for it.
story_hooks: A pair of these gloves is found at a chemical spill scene — one glove missing, the other stiff with dried blood and something that isn't acid.
A Tier 2 factory rep is quietly selling counterfeit Drekk gauntlets rated for conditions they can't handle — three workers have already been burned.
The wearer's left gauntlet has a serial number that matches a pair reported stolen from a sealed hazmat site two years ago.
